eyebrow: The T-SQL Development Course · Chapter Nine
subtitle: Lesson 100 · RCSI · Transactions, Locking, and Isolation Levels

eyebrow: A database setting -- not a session choice
code:
ALTER DATABASE AdventureWorks2012
SET READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT ON;
caption: Turned on once, by whoever administers the database.

code:
-- After RCSI is ON, this EXACT SAME query
-- behaves differently under the hood,
-- with no code change at all:
SELECT ProductID, Name, ListPrice
FROM Production.Product
WHERE ListPrice > 1000;
caption: Ordinary READ COMMITTED now reads a versioned copy, not a locked row.

eyebrow: What changes: no more blocking on writers
code:
-- WITHOUT RCSI: READ COMMITTED reads can be
--   BLOCKED by another session's uncommitted write.
-- WITH RCSI:    the read gets a last-committed
--   version immediately -- no waiting.
caption: The exact non-blocking benefit of SNAPSHOT, applied automatically.

eyebrow: The key difference from full SNAPSHOT
code:
-- RCSI:     fresh version EACH STATEMENT
--           (still allows nonrepeatable + phantom reads)
-- SNAPSHOT: ONE fixed version for the WHOLE transaction
caption: RCSI changes HOW reads happen -- not WHAT READ COMMITTED guarantees.
